memoryText: Let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is seated at the right hand of the throne of God.
readingInstruction: Today there is no new reading. This week you read the heart of Hebrews, the better priest, the better covenant, and the better sacrifice, followed by the call to faith and endurance. If you have time, reread Hebrews 12:1-3 slowly. Let it be a rest for your eyes, and let them settle on Jesus.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Hebrews 12:1-2 gathers the week into one picture. After chapters of argument about priests and sacrifices, the author puts you on the track and tells you where to look.

“Let us run with endurance the race that is set before us.” The race is set before you. God has not asked you to run someone else’s course. He has placed you where you are. And the race requires endurance, because it is long.

“Looking to Jesus.” The whole letter has been building to this. After describing his deity, his humanity, his priesthood, his covenant, and his sacrifice, the author says: look at him. When you are tired, look at him. When you are tempted, look at him. When you have failed, look at him.

“The founder and perfecter of our faith.” He started your faith, and he will finish it. You are not trusting in the strength of your own commitment. The one who began a good work in you will bring it to completion.

“For the joy that was set before him endured the cross.” He knew what lay ahead. The cross was real agony, and the joy was real too, because the joy was you. He saw the family he was gaining and he endured.

“And is seated at the right hand.” Again he sits. The race has been run, and the victory has been won. Say the verse aloud a few times today. When fatigue comes this week, let it send you to Jesus.
weekInReview:
This week brought you to the center of the book of Hebrews. You read about Melchizedek, the priest-king, and saw why the order of Aaron could never be final. You read about the better covenant that Jeremiah promised and the better sacrifice that Christ offered once for all. You saw the shadow and the reality side by side, and you heard the invitation to enter by the new and living way. You paused to consider the local church and what it means to be covenanted with a body of believers. You walked through the great chapter on faith, from Abel to the unnamed martyrs, and saw that all of them were waiting for something better. And you ended with a call to run with endurance, looking to Jesus, who is the founder and perfecter of faith.

The week’s message is simple. Everything the Old Testament pointed toward, Christ has done. You can come with confidence, you can endure with hope, and you can look to him.
reflectionQuestions: What does “once for all” mean for you personally? Hebrews says Christ’s sacrifice is complete and cannot be repeated or improved. Where do you still try to earn God’s approval, through performance, guilt, or striving? What would it look like to rest in a finished work?

How does Hebrews 12:2 change the way you think about suffering? Jesus endured the cross for the joy set before him. He knew what was on the other side. Think of a current difficulty. How might it look different if you saw it through the lens of the Savior who endured and is now seated in victory? What does it mean for you to look to him?

Who are the people in your life who stir you up to love and good works? Think of one person who encourages your faith, and one person you could encourage. Consider writing a note or sending a message today to say thank you or to offer prayer.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for offering a single sacrifice for sins and sitting down.
Tell him what you are trying to earn that he has already finished.
